title: Red Sox trading Marcelo Mayer to Giants for reliever Erik Miller: Sources
author: Johnny Flores Jr.
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

In an effort to bolster their pitching staff, the Boston Red Sox are trading former No. 4 overall pick Marcelo Mayer to the San Francisco Giants for left-hander Erik Miller. League sources told The Athletic. Boston will also receive minor league outfielder Carlos Gutierrez in the deal. The sources spoke under condition of anonymity to discuss a deal that had not been announced.

Mayer, who is currently on the IL with a bone stress reaction, has not played since June 25. His timeline for a return has not materialized.

In Miller, 28, Boston is receiving a controllable southpaw with above-average velocity and elite suppression of hard contact. He pairs a fastball that touches 99 mph with a wipeout slider that misses bats at an elite level. He was one of the game’s top lefties two years ago after the Giants got him for practically nothing from the Phillies.

There was a reason he was available, though, as he battled an assortment of injuries and command issues. Miller dealt with more elbow soreness last season, and although he’s stayed healthier this year, a high walk rate (6.1 per 9 innings) has prevented him from repeating every aspect of his success in 2024. Miller will be eligible for arbitration next year and won’t be a free agent until 2030.

The other piece Boston receives in the deal, Gutierrez, is a 21-year-old who is hitting .271 with an .826 OPS in 83 games at High A this season.

From a Giants perspective, Mayer is an exciting acquisition and a bigger get than one might expect for a reliever. He was one of the game’s top prospects a year ago and, assuming his rehab from a stress reaction in his forearm goes well, he becomes an immediate solution for the Giants after they dealt second baseman Luis Arraez to Philadelphia.

Mayer also plays shortstop, and if the Giants determine that he can handle the position better than Willy Adames, it could lead to some difficult conversations.

Mayer, the Red Sox’s first-round pick in 2021, debuted last season, but struggled to find his footing in the majors. Defensively gifted, Mayer strengthened the team at third base last year and played well at second and short this year but couldn’t find his rhythm at the plate.

Last season, after debuting in May when Alex Bregman was on the IL, Mayer took over as the starting third baseman. His year was cut short with a wrist injury in August.

This season, Mayer was the starting second baseman but landed on the IL in June with a forearm stress reaction and has just started swinging a bat.

Mayer seemed to be getting squeezed out of late.  Last week, the Red Sox acquired infielder Curtis Mead to play second base in the long term. Mead broke his wrist in his first game with Boston, but his acquisition signaled reduced playing time for Mayer. Meanwhile, the rise of top prospect Franklin Arias, a shortstop who debuted at Triple-A last week, furthered that notion. Evaluators see Arias as an even better defender than Mayer.

This story will be updated.
